  "text": "The hand paused. Whoever sat at that desk had heard him too.

Mara pressed her thumb against the glass.

“Is that tomorrow?”

The ferryman watched the open door across the river.

“Not if you put it down.”

In the mirror, her older hand resumed writing. There was a scar across its knuckles, pale and puckered. Mara looked at her own unmarked skin.

“What does it say?”

“You’ll have to turn it over.”

She almost obeyed. Then she noticed his hands: clenched at his sides, the nails driven deep into his palms.

“You can’t touch it.”

“No.”

“And you need me to read it.”

Across the river, Elias lowered his arm.

“Mara,” he called. “It’s cold.”

He had said that on the last evening, standing in their kitchen with his wet boots unlaced. She had told him there was firewood in the shed. By morning, the river had risen over the lower pasture, and the shed door was knocking against its frame.

She gripped the mirror harder.

“Tell me something,” she called. “What did you steal from the schoolmaster?”

The figure shifted its weight onto its good ankle.

“A pear.”

It was right. Everyone knew about the pear.

“What else?”

Beside her, the ferryman whispered, “Don’t.”

Elias stepped out of the doorway.

“A book,” he said.

Mara felt the brass edge cut her knuckles.

In the glass, the writing stopped. Her older hand lifted from the paper and turned palm upward, waiting.

“He wanted to learn,” Mara said.

The ferryman reached for her wrist.

She let the mirror fall."
